route.name: Hejaz Railway
route.description: Narrow gauge; partially operational in Jordan
route.notes: Jordan section documented + OSM-mapped (high); Saudi section known by station/km-post but sparse geometry (low). Total length ~1,300–1,320 km.  [established] 1908 = completion to Medina (first train Aug, ceremony 1 Sep 1908); ordered 1900.  [route] CORRECTIONS applied to the project list (km-posts from Damascus, per the Hejaz railway source): (1) Al-'Ula / Mada’in Salih order FIXED — Mada’in Salih (Hegra) is ~22 km NORTH of Al-'Ula, so southbound it comes FIRST (Mada’in Salih -> Al-'Ula), as you suspected. (2) Dahr al-Hajj, Akhdar (Qal’at al-Akhdar), Al-Khanzira and Al-Muazzam were listed AFTER Mada’in Salih/Al-'Ula but actually lie BETWEEN Tabuk and Mada’in Salih — moved north to their km-post positions. (3) DUPLICATES merged: Ziza = Jiza (Al-Jizah / Qal’at Zizya); Akhdar = Al-Akhdar (Qal’at al-Akhdar); Muaddham = Al-Muazzam (Al-Mu’azzam). (4) Khan Dannun placed between Damascus and Kiswe. (5) 'Wadi Rutm' Arabic corrected (وادي رتم, not وادي رم / Wadi Rum).  [completeness] The full historic line had ~100+ stations; many small desert halts documented by the Hejaz source (El-Hazim, Al-Muhtatab, Wadi al-Athily, Khamisa, Khashm Sana’a, Dar al-Hamra, Zumurrud, Bir Jadid, Stabl Antar, Bir Nassif, etc.) are NOT yet added — available on request.  [coordinates] Saudi-section coordinates are rough north-south estimates pending OSM / historical-map verification; km-posts (from Damascus) are the more reliable positional data there. Jebab & Al-Qasr added and route-less Libban wired in, per GSGS 2061/9 (1916).
route.history: The Hejaz Railway (1,050 mm), ordered 1900 by Sultan Abdül Hamid II and reaching Medina on 1 September 1908, ran ~1,300 km from Damascus via Deraa, Amman and Ma'an to Medina. It was the only railway built, owned and operated by the Ottoman state (funded by the treasury and pan-Islamic donations), chiefly engineered by Heinrich Meissner, and cut the pilgrimage from ~40 days to about five. It never reached Mecca, stopping at Medina.
